Subject: Committed drawdown ratchet & fallback plan

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising. As we kick off budgeting for H2 and into next year, the procurement team asked me to get clarity on how a multi-year committed spend would work operationally with Redwood. A few things we'd like to understand: 

- For a 3-year committed prepay (annual wallets with drawdown), do you have a standard "ratchet" that adjusts discount tiers based on trailing usage? If so, how is that calculated and when does it trigger?
- What are the typical ramp schedules Redwood accepts in year one (e.g., front-loaded credits vs. even monthly drawdown)?
- Is there a repurchase/true-up window for unused credits at year-end or on termination (we often have lumpy usage and need predictable accounting treatment)?
- If usage materially underperforms (e.g., <60% of committed run-rate), what fallback remedies exist from Redwood's side (reclaiming credits, replenishment fees, etc.)?

We have an internal target of 3.2M tokens/month in year one with a fast growth case up to 6.5M/month by year three. Happy to share a rough profile if it helps. Attaching our draft SOW so you can see the scope and expected call volume.

Can you send a one-page summary of options and an example drawdown schedule (monthly cadence) that shows the discount math and any penalties/repurchase mechanics? Would like to review with procurement next week.

Thanks,

Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Partnerships, Storify

Hi Liam (and Priya),

Great to hear this is progressing — thanks for the context and the SOW. Attached is a short template that shows two recommended structures and the math that governs the ratchet/true-up. High level options we typically offer: 

Option A — 3-year Term (frontloaded ladder)
- Yearly prepay (deposited up front into a wallet).
- Term discount: 15% off list for a 3-year commitment (applies to consumed token spend).
- Ratchet: quarterly usage review. If trailing 3-month usage < 70% of the committed monthly run-rate, holdback into escrow and apply a replenishment fee.

Option B — Annual Prepay with Monthly Drawdown (preferred for lumpy adopters)
- Annual wallet funded at the start of each 12-month period.
- Term discount: 10% off list for annual prepay.
- Drawdown cadence: daily continuous drawdown with monthly reconciliation and an annual true-up (repurchase allowed within 30 days of year-end).

Operational notes / questions for you:
- Can you share your expected month-by-month profile for year one (a simple 12-row CSV or the attached template is perfect).
- Do you expect material seasonality or one-off spikes tied to launches?

I've CC'd Karthik so he can weigh in on the replenishment fee and any legal language we should surface. Plan: if the template looks sensible, we can turn it into an SOW redline and DocuSign link ahead of your procurement meeting.

Attachments: redwood_commit_schedule_template.xlsx

Subject: Fwd: Storify SOW / drawdown ask — pricing calc (internal)

Internal note (do not forward externally)

Forwarding Liam's ask and the template I sent — procurement will want a concrete fallback clause. My preliminary proposal:

- Ratchet trigger: trailing 3-month usage < 65% of committed monthly run-rate -> move unconsumed funds into escrow and apply a replenishment fee of 5% of reclaimed credits. 
- Repurchase window: customer can repurchase escrowed credits within 60 days at the original effective discount rate (no laddering). If they do not repurchase within 60 days, escrowed credits convert to service credit that Redwood can reallocate.
- Yearly true-up: allow a 30-day true-up window at year-end; we reconcile consumed vs. committed and issue a single true-up invoice/refund.

Points for Karthik / Marissa: is 5% too punitive? Legal will push back on "convert to service credit" wording — we might need a time-boxed remediation period and an explicit right to terminate for chronic underuse. Also need to think about accounting for revenue recognition on frontloaded wallets.

I'll draft language for the SOW if you both think the commercial mechanics look reasonable.

Irene

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 14:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Storify SOW / drawdown ask — pricing calc (internal)

Irene — thanks for the summary. A few suggested adjustments before we present to procurement: 

- Reduce replenishment fee to 3% (keeps the stick but lowers negotiation friction).
- Set ratchet trigger at trailing 3-month usage < 60% for the first 12 months, then 70% thereafter — gives them runway to ramp.
- Offer a 6-month ramp credit in year one (10% of year-one commit returned as a non-refundable ramp allowance applied to first 6 months).
- Add an upside incentive: if normalized usage > 120% of commit for any rolling 6-month period, invoice a retroactive additional 2% usage credit to the customer (basically a variable rebate structure).

I've attached a quick breakout with scenarios (low / expected / high). Final ask: include explicit language that repurchased escrowed credits are billed at the effective prepay discount (no penalty on repurchase price) to keep accounting simple.

Agree we should avoid "convert to service credit" as a unilateral right — propose we include a remediation period (30 days) and then a specific recovery path.

Attaching: pricing_breakout_v2.csv

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Hi Liam / Priya — appreciate the patience while we scoped internal mechanics. Below is a concise commercial summary and the operational drawdown plan we recommend for Storify. If this matches procurement expectations we will convert into an SOW and send a DocuSign link.

Summary (recommended):
- Term: 3-year committed arrangement with annual wallets funded at the start of each year.
- Year 1 commit: 38M tokens (funded up front). Year 2/3: TBD based on signed schedule but we will provide a draft in the SOW.
- Discount: 15% term discount applied to consumed tokens for customers who sign a 3-year prepay.
- Ramp allowance: 10% of Year 1 wallet applied as a non-refundable ramp credit (applies to months 1–6).

Drawdown mechanics / governance:
- Continuous daily drawdown from the wallet with monthly reconciliation.
- Annual true-up: 30-day window after year-end to repurchase any shortfall or request a refund per the SOW.
- Ratchet / underuse fallback: trailing 3-month usage < 60% of committed monthly run-rate during year 1 triggers an escalation. We will move excess unconsumed credits into an escrow account and allow a 60-day repurchase window at the original effective discount. If not repurchased within 60 days, both parties will enter a 30-day remediation period before any conversion or termination actions.
- Replenishment fee (if customer requests immediate replenishment of escrowed credits): 3% of the replenished amount.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you are comfortable with the ratchet trigger (60% in year 1) and the 60-day repurchase window.
2) If confirmed, we'll prepare a redline SOW (attaching a draft) and issue a DocuSign link for signatures.
3) Schedule an executive procurement call for next Wednesday if you'd like to finalize the commercial terms live.
